title: Why Dropshipping Won't Make You Rich (Even With Sales)

beats.text: Dave made three thousand dollars in sales. Then he checked his bank account. He was down one thousand five hundred forty six dollars.
His product was a glowing cat lamp. He charged thirty dollars, and the supplier shipped it straight to the customer.
The store looked successful on the screen. But sales were not profit, and Dave was about to find out why.
The supplier charged twelve dollars per lamp. From a thirty dollar sale, Dave had eighteen dollars left.
Payment processing took one dollar and twenty cents. That left sixteen dollars and eighty cents before ads, refunds, or anything else.
Dave paid for ads. Every click cost fifty cents, even when the person clicked away without buying.
One hundred clicks cost fifty dollars. Only two people bought, so advertising alone cost twenty five dollars per customer.
The ad platform got paid. The store platform got paid. The supplier got paid. Dave was the one covering the shortfall.
Then orders arrived late. Customers asked for refunds, and some disputed the charges with their banks. Those losses came on top.
Dave opened his calculator. He had just sixteen dollars and eighty cents available to acquire a customer before he started losing money.
But each customer cost him twenty five dollars in ads. That was a loss of at least eight dollars and twenty cents per sale, before refunds.
Dave switched off the ads and shut the laptop. Three thousand dollars in sales meant nothing if every sale made him poorer.
